note: No corpus. The input is the run report `e2e/bench-journey-day1.spec.ts` writes, and this file is the contract between the two so neither has to guess at the other's shape.

reportShape.completed: 1 when the whole first session finished, absent when the spec never ran
reportShape.studentTaps: controls the student pressed, including the two navigations they make themselves; typing is not a tap
reportShape.totalSeconds: wall clock for the run, including the app's own network and the runner's waits
reportShape.stepCount: how many steps the spec walked — checked against expectedStepCount so a shortened journey cannot report a higher signal count
reportShape.stepsWithNextSignal: steps where the page told the student what to do next before they had to work it out
reportShape.measuredAt: ISO instant, so a stale report can be recognised

ageNote: A report older than this is treated as absent rather than scored. A green `completed: 1` from last week, reported against today's commit, is a passing gate that measured nothing.

designFloors.note: The design's proposed floors (spec section 4.6, marked with a dagger): 8 taps or fewer, 90 seconds or less of scripted interaction. Neither is set as a floor yet — no CI run has established today's real number, and the authoring worktree had no dev server or DATABASE_URL to establish one (the standing 'a worktree has no .env.local' gotcha). Enumerating the controls on the path suggests roughly ten, so adopting 8 sight-unseen would red the gate on a product fact nobody has agreed to act on. See the runbook's open items: set the baseline from the first CI run, then floor.

howToRun: npx tsx scripts/seed-e2e-users.ts   # idempotent; also clears login rate limits
npm run dev   # or npm run start against a build
workersNote: --workers=1 is not optional, and it is not sufficient on its own. /api/auth/login applies TWO limiters: login:<ip> at 10 attempts per 15 minutes, and login:user:<studentId> at 5 — and since every e2e spec signs in as the same handful of fixture accounts, the PER-USER cap binds first (measured: the 429 lands on the 6th attempt, not the 11th). The buckets are RateLimitEntry rows, so they outlive the webServer and are shared by every `playwright test` invocation against one database. Re-run `npx tsx scripts/seed-e2e-users.ts` before a collection pass that follows another suite run — it is idempotent and clears the login buckets, and it refuses any non-local, non-CI database by construction (src/lib/e2e-seed-guard.ts). CI does exactly this between its gate step and its collection step.
